newsitem.title: FRANCE: Club Med H1 net loss 413 mln Ffr.
newsitem.headline: Club Med H1 net loss 413 mln Ffr.

text.p: (Figures in millions of French francs unless stated)
Net interest expense** expense 88 vs expense 144
Net profit befoore minority interests 410 vs 101
NOTE - *H1 1997 operating profit is after taking into account 138 million francs in non-recurring charges.
**Net interest expense in H1 1996 (144 million francs) included non-recurring charges of 40 million francs.

Leisure and holiday group Club Mediterranee, which carried out a 820 million franc restructuring in 1996, said it was re-evaluating its strategy. "At this stage, however, it was found necessary to implement some key accounting measures without delay. The total cost of these measures amounts to 630 million francs," it said in a statement with the first half results.

"The finalised strategic plan will be presented to the Supervisory Board by the end of the year. The plan may involve additional provisions and charges which, in any case, should amount to less than the 630 million francs recorded in the first half," it said.

Within the increase in turnover, Club Med cited the following three factors: the negative impact of changes in the scope of consolidation, as deconsolidation of the South American activities exceeded turnover recognised from Forum Voyages; a favourable currency effect from a stronger dollar; a positive price effect, as volumes remained more or less flat.
At comparable scope of consolidation and exchange rates, turnover rose by 2.2 percent.
Net interest expense declined as a result of the favourable rate environment.

"Exceptional items included costs related to the examination of assets and risks as of this date, which mainly involved the new software system, the valuation of land and the recognition of legal risks" it said.
It said that in spite of the results, "the financial situation remains healthy with a financial debt limited to 2.4 billion francs for 3.5 billion francs shareholders' equity".
